help.intro: A product is the style - the thing you name and file. What is actually sold, priced and counted is its variant, and every product has at least one. Two statuses sit side by side on each row and mean different things: workflow is where the record stands editorially, sale status is whether it is sellable today.
help.step_1_title: Give it a name in every language
help.step_1_body: A product carries no code of its own - the codes belong to its variants. What identifies it is the translation: the slug is unique per language across live products, and the check ignores deleted ones, so deleting a product releases its slug for reuse and restoring it afterwards fails if something else has taken it.
help.step_2_body: At least one is required, and not for tidiness: the attribute form a product is asked to fill in is resolved from its categories, so one filed under nothing has no form. The public address does not depend on them - it is /products/<product-slug>, the slug alone. Only product-type categories are offered.
help.step_3_body: Name and slug are required per language, and a language may appear only once. The slug is lower-cased on save and is the public URL segment, so changing it on a live product changes the address customers already have.
help.step_4_title: Add the variants - this is where price and stock live
help.step_4_body: At least one variant, exactly one marked default, and no two sharing a SKU. Prices exclude VAT and are per currency; min price is the floor a stacked discount may not resolve below, so it cannot exceed the price. Low stock threshold only means anything while track stock is on. A product with nothing to vary still needs exactly one - that is the normal case, not a workaround.
help.step_5_title: Set the catalog window, and let sale status follow
help.step_5_body: Available from, available until and discontinued at describe the product's life in the catalog, and available until must be after available from. Sale status is not a field you set: a scheduled job recomputes it from those three dates, so it can lag an edit by a few minutes rather than flipping as you save. Discontinued is permanent.
help.step_6_body: Draft goes to pending review; pending review goes either to ready or back for revision; revision required returns to pending review. Ready is terminal - nothing leads out of it, so a product that reaches it cannot be walked back. Workflow is changed by these buttons, never by the edit form, because each move is checked against that map.
help.note: Deleting a product is a soft delete and works from any workflow state. Use Show deleted to find one and restore it. Bundles are a known gap: setting composition to bundle needs components, which cannot be picked here yet, and the API refuses to save a bundle without them - build those through the API for now.

text.no_intervals_the_product_can_be: No intervals - the product can be ordered at any time while it is available.
text.selected_categories_declare_no_product_a: Selected categories declare no product attributes.
text.the_wording_one_set_per_language: The wording, one set per language - name, slug, description and the SEO meta. The slug is the whole public address (eg: /products/my-slug), so changing it moves the page.
text.the_reference_price_is_below_the: The reference price is below the sale price, so it advertises an increase rather than a saving.
text.price_the_bundle_first_a_delta: Price the bundle first - a delta needs a market to be quoted in.
text.placeholder_component_search: Search by SKU or product name…
text.no_base_components_yet_a_bundle: No base components yet. A bundle needs one with a quantity of 2, or two different ones.
text.nothing_optional_the_bundle_is_a: Nothing optional. The bundle is a fixed kit as it stands.
text.common_details_for_all_the_product: Common details for all the product variants. Specific attributes are set on the Variants tab.
text.this_product_is_a_bundle_its: This product is a bundle. Its name, content, categories, availability and price are edited here; its components are not - they are managed on the bundle page.
text.applies_to_the_whole_product_every: Applies to the whole product - every variant is taxed at this rate.
text.pricing_and_inventory_are_managed_at: Pricing and inventory are managed at the variant level, not the product level. Define a separate variant for each distinct configuration (e.g., different size, color, etc). Products that have no variations must still have exactly one default variant.
text.a_question_asked_at_order_time: A question asked at order time, and what each answer does to the price (eg: Extra bacon, a choice of crust, etc).
text.each_answer_moves_the_variant_price: Each answer moves the variant price by its delta, per market. A negative delta is legitimate - declining something the price already includes.
text.a_question_has_to_offer_something: A question has to offer something - add at least one answer.
text.no_questions_the_product_is_ordered: No questions - the product is ordered as it is, with nothing for the customer to choose.
text.off_for_anything_not_counted_a: Off for anything not counted - a dish, a download. The two settings beside it apply only while it is on, and are cleared when it is turned off.
text.each_product_variant_has_its_own: Each product variant has its own prices.
text.a_product_is_priced_and_stocked: A product is priced and stocked through its variants, so at least one is required - add a single variant if there is nothing to vary.
text.no_restriction_orderable_at_any_time: No restriction - orderable at any time while available.
text.no_questions_ordered_as_it_is: No questions - ordered as it is.
text.no_tracked_variants: No variant of this product tracks stock.
text.attribute_declare_bundle: Declare a new attribute for one of this bundle's categories
text.attribute_declare_product: Declare a new attribute for one of this product's categories
text.attributes_need_category_bundle: Please select at least one category to add bundle attributes.
text.attributes_need_category_product: Please select at least one category to view product attributes.
text.availability_dates_hint_bundle: The dates below decide whether the bundle is listed at all; the intervals under them decide when a listed bundle can be ordered (eg: a lunch menu, weekdays 12:00–15:00).
text.availability_dates_hint_product: The dates below decide whether the product is listed at all; the intervals under them decide when a listed product can be ordered (eg: a lunch menu, weekdays 12:00–15:00).
text.availability_intervals_hint_bundle: One interval per day, recurring within that life. A bundle outside its hours is still listed, just not orderable right now.
text.availability_intervals_hint_product: One interval per day, recurring within that life. A product outside its hours is still listed, just not orderable right now.
text.hint_sale_price: {{term}} is what the customer is charged, excluding VAT.
text.hint_reference_price: {{term}} is the usual price the sale is measured against - shown to signal a saving.
text.hint_minimum_price: The discounted price cannot drop below the set {{term}}
text.hint_cost_price: What the goods cost you, in {{currency}} - never charged, never shown to customers.
text.note_below_cost: A discount may resolve to {{floor}}, below the {{cost}} this variant cost.
text.note_unknown_rate: No {{base}} rate for {{currency}} - this floor cannot be checked against the cost price.
text.cardinality_at_least: Required - at least {{min}}, no upper limit.
text.cardinality_max_hint: Leave the maximum empty for no upper limit.
text.label_included_how: Included outright, or through a choice
text.choice_intro: A choice is what says {{exactly}}. It is not optional - the bundle always contains one candidate, and the customer only decides which - so its candidates are {{base}} components naming it below. It needs at least two of them.
text.base_components_hint: Always included, and covered by the bundle price - either outright or through a choice, which always takes one of its candidates. Two units contained outright, or the bundle is a single product; a candidate does not count, since which one is taken is the customer's.
text.base_components_delta_hint: A candidate carries an adjustment per market: taking it adds its own price plus that adjustment. Since the bundle price already covers the candidate, the adjustment is usually its whole price, negative, so nothing is added.
text.optional_components_hint: The customer may take these or leave them, up to the quantity on each.
text.optional_components_delta_hint: Every unit taken adds the component's own price plus the adjustment on its row. Usually negative - the discount for taking it inside the kit.
